answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed on proven misbehavior, like a lagoon admitting only boats with real cargo. Newcomers then earn trust slowly through verified work: an orchard model where reputation grows only as tasks are completed honestly over time, so spinning up thousands of fake identities costs far more than any single fraud gains. A shared reputation graph isolates bad actors on one island of distrust instead of letting them poison the whole network, making coordinated fakery costly and easy to quarantine.
